newsitem.title: INDIA: Anti-Miss World protest jams Bangalore traffic.
newsitem.headline: Anti-Miss World protest jams Bangalore traffic.

text.p: Protestors against the Miss World beauty pageant coming to India blocked traffic in the heart of Bangalore for more than three hours on Tuesday.
The demonstrators heard more fiery speeches reiterating threats to lay siege to the cricket stadium in this southern Indian city where Miss World will be crowned on November 23.

The Bangalore police plan to mount a massive security operation involving more than 12,000 police officers to safeguard the event, which had an estimated television audience of two billion people last year.

"Let us see how many bullets and guns they will use. Can they stop over 200,000 people from storming the stadium. We will not allow the show, we are clear about that," Shashikala, leader of the Mahila Jagran (Forum to Awaken Women) said after members of her organisation clashed with police.
Her group has already threatened that some members will commit suicide by self-immolation to wreck the beauty contest.
Demonstrators belonging to the militant traditionalist Farmers Association staged a sit-in outside the Karnataka state government headquarters in Bangalore, after failing to break a police cordon.

Senior local members of the main opposition conservative Hindu-nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party joined the protest, which dispersed after the crowd had shouted slogans against the government and police for supporting the Miss World contest.

"Over 100,000 people from all over India will lay seige to the stadium to prevent the show. The pageant is an affront on Indian culture," Ananth Kumar, member of Parliament from Bangalore and a senior BJP leader said.

The opponents of Miss World are also trying to block the event through the courts by contesting the right of the state government and Amitabh Bachchan Corp Ltd, the Indian organisers of this year's contest, to hold the show.
